skills.name: Classify triangles
skills.wrong_turn: Isosceles means at least two equal sides, so every equilateral triangle is isosceles too.
skills.rule: By sides: equilateral, isosceles, scalene. By angles: acute, right, obtuse, equiangular.

skills.name: Triangle sum proof
skills.wrong_turn: Draw the parallel through a vertex, to the opposite side. The alternate interior angles must sit at that vertex for the proof to work.
skills.rule: Triangle sum theorem: m∠A+m∠B+m∠C=180°. Proof: draw the parallel through one vertex.

skills.name: Exterior angle theorem
skills.wrong_turn: Use the two remote angles, not the one next door. The exterior angle and its neighbour add to 180°.
skills.rule: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.

skills.name: Congruent figures
skills.wrong_turn: Letter order is the match-up. If △ABC ≅ △DEF, then AB matches DE, not EF, however the picture is turned.
skills.rule: Congruent polygons have all corresponding sides and all corresponding angles congruent.

skills.name: SSS
skills.wrong_turn: The matching sides must pair up exactly. Sides 3, 4, 5 and 3, 4, 6 share two lengths, but that isn't SSS.
skills.rule: SSS: if three sides of one triangle are congruent to three sides of another, the triangles are congruent.

skills.name: SAS
skills.wrong_turn: The angle must lie between the two sides. Two sides and a non-included angle (SSA) can give two different triangles.
skills.rule: SAS: two sides and the included angle congruent give congruent triangles.

skills.name: ASA
skills.wrong_turn: The side must connect the two angles. Two angles and a side not between them is AAS, a different case.
skills.rule: ASA: two angles and the included side congruent give congruent triangles.

skills.name: AAS
skills.wrong_turn: Angles alone never prove congruence: AAA gives the same shape, possibly a different size. At least one pair of sides must match.
skills.rule: AAS: two angles and a non-included side congruent give congruent triangles.

skills.name: HL
skills.wrong_turn: HL is only for right triangles. In other triangles, two sides and a non-included angle (SSA) don't prove congruence.
skills.rule: HL: right triangles with congruent hypotenuses and one pair of congruent legs are congruent.

skills.name: CPCTC proofs
skills.wrong_turn: Prove the triangles congruent first. CPCTC can't supply the sides you need for SAS.
skills.rule: CPCTC: corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent.

skills.name: Isosceles triangles
skills.wrong_turn: Base angles are opposite the equal sides. If AB = AC, then ∠B ≅ ∠C, not ∠A ≅ ∠B.
skills.rule: Base angles theorem: if two sides are congruent, the angles opposite them are congruent, and conversely.

skills.name: Triangle inequality

steps.a: sum of two sides beats the third

skills.wrong_turn: Test the two shortest sides against the longest. 3, 4, 8 fails because 3 + 4 < 8, even though 4 + 8 > 3.
skills.rule: Each side is less than the sum of the other two: a+b>c.

skills.name: Midsegment theorem
skills.wrong_turn: The midsegment is half the side it's parallel to, not half a side it touches. If MN ∥ BC, then MN = ½BC.
skills.rule: A midsegment is parallel to the third side and half as long.

skills.name: Points of concurrency
skills.wrong_turn: The centroid is 2/3 of the way from a vertex to the opposite midpoint, not halfway. On a median of 9, it is 6 from the vertex.
skills.rule: Perpendicular bisectors meet at the circumcenter; angle bisectors at the incenter; medians at the centroid; altitudes at the orthocenter.
